about:
# Fireside Tales

## The vision

Fireside Tales is a rumor mill for World of Warcraft: Forever: a big, ever-growing collection of stories and legends that anyone can sit down and tell at a campfire. It's a fun side thing to the game, for people who want to tell a tale or stop and listen to one.

If you're working on this project, whether you're a person or an AI, these are the goals that decide what to do:

- **Keep adding stories.** The collection is the product. There should be so many that you always have something new to tell, whenever you reach a fire.
- **Stories belong to everyone.** Zone, race, and class stories are welcome as long as they're generic enough for any character who fits to tell. Stories tied to one specific character stay out of the shared collection.
- **Your own stories are what make you care.** The built-in stories give everyone something to tell, but telling your own character's story is what gives a player buy-in. Adding your own has to be easy, probably with the help of an AI, and they stay yours to tell at the fire.
- **Stories work at a campfire.** Each one takes 60 seconds or less to tell, including the pauses that let people read. Add up each line's read cue from `TellerBar.lua` to estimate this: 3 seconds plus 1 for every 20 characters, between 4 and 14 per line.
- **The addon stays stupid simple.** Pick a story and press Speak. A new feature has to earn its place, and it shouldn't make that any harder.
- **Delight the players.** Favor whatever makes someone at the fire smile, lean in, or want to tell one of their own.

For now, all the stories ship in this one addon. Text is small, so it doesn't need separate story packs. It's published on [CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/fireside-tales). [Join us on Discord](https://discord.gg/GyrhmXnQTW) to share stories, report bugs and suggest ideas.

## What it is

An addon for telling stories at the campfire in World of Warcraft: Forever, one line at a time, using `/say` and `/e`. It works on Windows and macOS.

It comes in two halves:

- **The storytelling:** a story menu with filters, a small teller bar, favorites, and an evening list.
- **The stories:** a shared collection for every race, class, and zone, plus **Write Your Tales**, which helps you use an AI to write your own character's stories right from the game.
- **Community stories:** players contribute stories and rumors at [firesidetales.dev](https://firesidetales.dev/), and each week's are featured in the **Community** tab. The site's code is in [`site/`](https://github.com/death-walrus-studios/fireside-tales/blob/main/site/README.md), and `tools/build-community.mjs` writes them into `Community.lua`.

The addon never sends chat by itself. The game requires a key press or click for `/say` and `/e` outside instances, so every line waits for you to press Speak.

## Setup

1. Close the game and extract the zip into your AddOns folder, so its files end up in `AddOns/FiresideTales/`:

   - **Windows:** `C:\Program Files (x86)\World of Warcraft\_forever_\Interface\AddOns\`
   - **macOS:** `/Applications/World of Warcraft/_forever_/Interface/AddOns/`

   Create the `AddOns` folder if it isn't there. Your game may be installed somewhere else.

2. Start the game. If addons load individually, turn on Fireside Tales at the character screen.

3. Optional: bind keys under **Options > Keybindings > Fireside Tales** for Speak and the story menu. The on-screen buttons work without them.

## Telling a story

1. Click the book icon on the minimap, or type `/tales stories`. Drag the icon to move it around the minimap's edge.
2. Narrow the list with the filters, then pick a story to preview it. Scroll either pane with the mouse wheel. The reader shows each story's mood and roughly how long it takes to tell.
3. Press **Tell**. The menu shrinks to the teller bar, so you can see the fire again, and nothing is said yet. Press **Opener** to gather people first if you like, then **Speak** for each line.

Can't decide? **Tell a Tale** picks one for you: a story you haven't told yet, for a festival that's on, then about where you are, then one for your character, race, or class, then any other. At night in the game it reaches for spooky and dark tales first, and gentler ones by day. Press it again for a different one.

### The tabs

Tabs down the right side of the menu, like the character window's, sort the stories:

- **Your Tales**, with your character's portrait: only your character's own stories.
- **Stories**: everything else, described below.
- **Legends**: Warcraft's own stories, told in parts, with the one where you're standing first. Each part takes under a minute. When one ends, Speak becomes **Next part**, so you can stop for the night or keep going. Tell a Tale and the campfire prompt never start you partway through a legend.
- **Rumors and Whispers**: short things people swear they heard, with rumors about where you are first. Tell a Tale picks these too.

### Openers and closers

On the teller bar, before the first line, an **Opener** button gathers people with one line, like "Gather round, everyone. I've got one for you." When a story ends, **Closer** sends it off, matched to the story's mood. Hover either one to see exactly what it will say. Each is said only when you press it, once per story, and closers wait until the end of a legend rather than between its parts. They're in `Openers.lua`.

### Festivals

The Darkmoon Faire, Lunar Festival, Love is in the Air, Noblegarden, Children's Week, Midsummer, the Harvest Festival, Hallow's End, and Winter Veil each have their own stories, under **From: Festivals** all year. While one is on, an **On now** section opens at the top of the list and the campfire prompt mentions it. The addon reads the game's calendar, and if it can't, it knows the Darkmoon Faire opens the Monday after the first Friday of each month for a week, and the dates of Midsummer, Hallow's End, and Winter Veil.

### The campfire prompt

Sit down at a campfire and a small prompt pops up on the teller bar asking if you'd like to tell a story ("By the fire. Tell a tale?"). Press **Speak** to start it, **Another** for a different story, or close it. It appears once you have the fire's Welcoming Campfire or Cozy Fire buff and have stayed still for a few seconds. It asks once per fire, at most once every 5 minutes, never in combat, and not while the menu is open or a story is half told. If nobody takes the offer, it goes away after 30 seconds or when you leave the fire. `/tales fire` turns these offers off or back on.

### The teller bar

The bar shows the next line and your progress. After each line, a gold cue shows roughly how long people need to read it. It's only a suggestion, so **Speak** always works. **Menu** goes back to the list, and closing the menu partway through a story returns you to the bar.

The bar also shows up to three recent `/say` and `/e` lines from people nearby, each for 45 seconds, and it's shorter when there's nothing to show. A line that uses your name, or a plain emote aimed at you, turns gold and makes a sound. The game may hide chat from addons in instances, and the bar only listens while it's open.

### Stories told to someone

The **Target Someone First** section holds stories that use your listener's name. Target them, then press **Speak**, which stays unavailable until you do. The name stays the same for the rest of the story, even if your target changes, until you restart it.

### Favorites, told stories, and Tonight

- **Favorite** stars a story in the list.
- A story's title turns gray once you've spoken its last line. It stays in the same place, since your audience changes from night to night.
- **Add to Tonight** lines up stories in the order you add them, at the top of the list. When one ends, **Next story** loads the next without saying anything. The list stays until you remove stories or choose **Clear Tonight's list** from the **Show** filter.

These are saved separately for each character.

### Filters

Each story in the list has a colored square for its mood, matching the **Mood** filter, and roughly how many seconds it takes to tell on the right. Hover a story to see its mood, length, and when you last told it. In the reader, emotes are orange and speech is white.

Sections start closed, except Tonight, your current zone, and your character's own, so click a section's name to open or close it. Any filter opens every section that has a match.

The filters sit in one row above the list. They combine, and the count at the top shows how many stories match:

- **Search:** type any words. A story matches if its title, theme, mood, or text contains all of them, such as `bear` or `winter inn`.
- **From:** show only the stories for where you are, your character's own, your race's, your class's, the ones told to a target, the ones for everyone, or tales of places.
- **Mood:** Funny, Heartfelt, Dark, Action, Spooky, or Wise.
- **Show:** Favorites, stories you haven't told yet, stories you've added, or only Tonight's list.

**Clear** appears while a filter is on and resets all four.

**Restart** goes back to the first line. **Escape** closes the menu. Your place in a story is kept until you pick another or `/reload`.

### What's in the list

The Stories tab's list is built for whoever you're logged in as, in this order:

1. **Tonight**, if you've added any
2. **On now**, for a festival that's running
3. **Here in your zone**: tales of the zone you're in, plus any of your other stories that mention it or a place in it. It updates as you travel.
4. **Your character's tales**, matched by the character's first name. This section always lists all of them, so one that mentions your zone appears in both places.
5. **Race stories**, chosen from what the game reports
6. **Class stories**, chosen the same way
7. **Target Someone First**, told to one listener
8. **Shared stories**, available to everyone
9. **Festivals**, one section each
10. **Tales of other places**, grouped by zone

To teach a zone new place names, add them to `ns.ZoneTerms` in `StoryData.lua`.

## Writing your own stories

1. Press **Write Your Tales** in the menu, or type `/tales add`.
2. Optionally, write a sentence or two about your character. It's saved for next time, and without it the AI invents something. If you use [Total RP 3](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/total-rp-3), your current profile is already in the prompt: name, title, appearance, where you're from and live, what you're doing, and the start of your backstory. Use the box for anything else.
3. Press **Select Prompt**, copy it with Cmd+C or Ctrl+C, and paste it into any AI. Your character's name, race, class, and zone are already filled in.
4. Paste the AI's answer into the bottom box and press **Add**. It's fine to paste the whole reply.

Your stories appear under **`<name>`'s Tales**, near the top of the list. Anything you've added has a green-tinted title and says "added by you", and **Show: Added by me** lists just those. The window says how many it added, and why it skipped any. Read them before you tell them, since you're the one saying them out loud.

Pasted stories are saved with your account, outside the addon's folder, so updating the addon doesn't remove them. **Delete** in the menu removes a pasted story.

The addon's `prompts` folder has more prompts for a race or class, a zone, everyone, and stories told to someone by name. Their answers go in the same box.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/tales` or `/tales stories` | Open or close the story menu |
| `/tales help` | List the commands |
| `/tales add` | Open or close the Write Your Tales window |
| `/tales settings` | Open the Settings tab: story language and voices |
| `/tales voices` | Show which voices are on, and open the Settings tab |
| `/tales news` | Open or close What's New, which also opens once after each update |
| `/tales language` | Show or change the language stories are told in (German, French, Spanish, Russian, Korean, or English), as the Settings tab does |
| `/tales fire` | Turn the campfire prompt off or back on |
| `/tales minimap` | Show or hide the minimap icon |
| `/tales status` | Show who the addon thinks you are, and your story counts |

## Working on the addon

These commands need [PowerShell 7](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/scripting/install/installing-powershell), which also runs on macOS. To link the project into the game so edits load directly, run:

```powershell
./install-addon.ps1
```

Pass `-WowPath` if the game isn't in the default location. Restart the game after linking.

Built-in stories are in `addon/FiresideTales/stories/`, one file per section of the story menu:

- **Stories for everyone:** `shared/`, one file per heading, like `shared/GhostStories.lua`. Rumors are `shared/RumorsAndWhispers.lua`, which gets its own tab; keep them to about three lines.
- **Race and class stories:** `races/` and `classes/`, one file per race or class, like `races/Undead.lua` and `classes/Mage.lua`.
- **Zone stories:** `zones/`, one file per zone, like `zones/ElwynnForest.lua`.
- **Stories told to a target:** `Targeted.lua`. Write `{target}` where the name goes, and describe only what the teller does, never what the listener does or feels.
- **Festival stories:** `festivals/`, one file per festival. Each file's list name matches a festival in `Seasons.lua`, which also holds how each festival is recognized.
- **Legends:** `Legends.lua`. Each legend has a zone, a title, a one-line `summary`, and its `parts`, which are stories in order. Keep them true to the game's own lore, list your sources above each one, and retell rather than quote.
- **Riddles** are in `Riddles.lua`, and this week's community stories in `Community.lua`, which is written from the site.
- **Your own character's stories** go in `characters/`, which stays on your computer and out of git.

A new file has to be listed in `FiresideTales.toc` (with backslashes, like `stories\zones\Westfall.lua`), and the game only picks it up after a full restart. `tools/check-stories.ps1` says if one is missing.

Each story needs a `title`, a `mood` (`funny`, `heartfelt`, `dark`, `action`, `spooky`, or `wise`), and `lines`. Shared stories also need a `theme`.

Stories are told sitting around a campfire, so write emotes that work while seated. Act out a past event with your hands and upper body, rather than standing, walking, kneeling, or crouching. Each line is one chat message, so keep it under 255 bytes. Emote lines begin with a verb because the game adds your name, and `|` isn't allowed in chat text.

Edits to these files load with `/reload`. A brand-new file needs a game restart and an entry in `FiresideTales.toc`. To catch mistakes before you load them, run:

```powershell
./tools/check-stories.ps1
```

To test the whole addon outside the game, run the harness with [LuaJIT](https://luajit.org/). See [tools/harness/README.md](https://github.com/death-walrus-studios/fireside-tales/blob/main/tools/harness/README.md).

```sh
luajit tools/harness/harness.lua
```

### Other languages

The addon's interface follows the game client's language, and stories are told in the player's story language (`/tales language`, the client's by default). Translations live in `translations/<language>/` as JSON and are built into `addon/FiresideTales/locales/` by `node tools/i18n/build.mjs`, which also checks them. A story with any string untranslated stays in English. Wrap new interface text in `L["..."]`, and text the addon itself says in chat in `ns.Locale.T("...")`. See [docs/translation-guide.md](https://github.com/death-walrus-studios/fireside-tales/blob/main/docs/translation-guide.md).

### Local stories

Any other story files in `.gitignore` stay on the computer that has them, with no copy on GitHub. The `.toc` lists them, and the game skips any that aren't there. To add a new one, add it to `.gitignore` and `FiresideTales.toc`.

### Releasing

Pushing a version tag publishes to CurseForge and GitHub. See [docs/RELEASING.md](https://github.com/death-walrus-studios/fireside-tales/blob/main/docs/RELEASING.md).

### Building the zip

This builds `dist/FiresideTales-<version>.zip` with the addon, shared stories, and prompts, and without local stories:

```powershell
./tools/build-release.ps1
```

To update, replace the whole `FiresideTales` folder with the new one. Pasted stories, favorites, and history aren't stored there, so they stay.

## Removing it

Delete the `FiresideTales` folder from `AddOns`. If you linked it instead, this removes the link and leaves your project files in place:

```powershell
./install-addon.ps1 -Uninstall
```

## License

The code and stories are under the [MIT License](https://github.com/death-walrus-studios/fireside-tales/blob/main/LICENSE).

## Requirements

The WoW: Forever client (interface `16001`) on Windows or macOS. Update `## Interface` in `FiresideTales.toc` when the client's version changes, or the game will mark the addon out of date.

releases.name: Fireside Tales 1.11.0
releases.notes:
## 1.11.0

- Added German, French, Spanish (Spain and Latin America), Russian, and Korean.
- The menus follow your game's language. Choose the language for your stories in Settings or with /tales language.
- Renamed the Voices tab to Settings. Added /tales settings.
- Write Your Tales now asks for stories in your story language.
- Voices still play in English for every language.
- The narrator's voice is new. Update the Narrator pack to hear it.
- Restart the game after updating.

## 1.10.6

- Added a What's New window that opens once after each update. Reopen it with /tales news or from the story menu.

## 1.10.5

- All race voices are new and improved. Update your voice packs to hear them.

## 1.10.4

- Reorganized the built-in stories by menu section. Nothing changes in game.

## 1.10.3

- Community stories now change completely each week, and past weeks' stories are no longer listed.

## 1.10.2

- The voice packs now show as optional add-ons on Fireside Tales' CurseForge page.

## 1.10.1

- Voices now come in a pack for each race, plus the narrator and community stories, since CurseForge limits each download to about 500 MB.
- Voices sound clearer.
- The Voices tab groups the packs by faction, with a Get button for each group.

## 1.10.0

- Added voices: stories told nearby are read aloud in the voice of the teller's race. The voice packs are free, separate downloads.
- Added a Voices tab to the story menu, with each pack, who reads (race voices or the narrator), your own stories, and a sample.
- Added /tales voices.
- Restart the game after updating.

## 1.9.2

- New Community stories for the week of November 17, by Garvin Flintwatch.

## 1.9.1

- Fixed the Delete and Restart buttons overlapping.

## 1.9.0

- Added Edit for your own tales, so you can change one without pasting it again.

## 1.8.0

- Added a Riddles tab with 22 riddles. Ask one at the fire, and whoever says the answer first wins.
- If nobody gets it, press Speak for a hint, then again for the answer.
- Restart the game after updating.

## 1.7.1

- Removed the placeholder stories from the Community tab.

## 1.7.0

- Added 10 legends: Sylvanas, Anduin and Varian, Mount Hyjal, Tirion and Eitrigg, Grom Hellscream, Uther, Anduin Lothar, Tyrande, and two Skyborne histories.
- Single-part legends no longer show "part 1 of 1".
- **Special thanks to tmillerpdx for writing all ten!**

## 1.6.0

- Added a Community tab with new stories from players every week.
- Added Contribute a Story, which points you to firesidetales.dev.
- You'll get a message in chat when one of your stories is featured.
- Renamed Write My Story to Write Your Tales.
- Restart the game after updating.

## 1.5.0

- Added side tabs for Your Tales, Stories, Legends, and Rumors and Whispers.
- Tell now puts a story on the teller bar first, so you can start with an Opener and finish with a Closer.
- Added 5 legends: Stalvan, In Dreams, the Tower of Althalaxx, Dartol's Rod, and Onyxia.
- Added 24 rumors, 7 Winter Veil stories, and a night story for every zone.
- Fixed 27 stories with lines that didn't make sense.

## 1.4.0

- Added 27 festival stories. They show up first while their festival is on.
- Tell a Tale picks spooky and dark stories at night.
- Write My Story can use your Total RP 3 profile.
- Fixed the campfire prompt not showing at WoW: Forever campsites.

## 1.3.0

- Added Tell a Tale, which picks a story you haven't told yet.
- Added a campfire prompt when you sit by a fire. Turn it off with `/tales fire`.
- The reader shows about how long a story takes.

## 1.2.0

- Added 46 action and wise stories. Every zone has at least four now.
- The version number shows in the menu and in `/tales status`.

## 1.1.1

- Removed the pop-up that suggested lines after quests, level-ups, and deaths.

## 1.1.0

- Added 81 stories, including the first ones for Moonglade, Deadwind Pass, Mount Hyjal, the Riverglades, and Shen'dralas.
- Removed 16 duplicate stories.
- Every emote works while sitting now.
- Fixed some lore details for WoW: Forever.

## 1.0.1

- Added sounds for windows, picking a story, and filters.

## 1.0.0

- First release, with over 400 stories for every race, class, and zone.
- Write My Story helps you write your own character's stories with any AI.
- Search, filters, favorites, and a list for tonight.
